overview: REA Group is a multinational digital advertising business specialising in property, operating Australia's leading residential and commercial property websites realestate.com.au and realcommercial.com.au, alongside share-accommodation site flatmates.com.au and data business PropTrack. The Group also owns Mortgage Choice (mortgage broking franchise), CampaignAgent (vendor-paid advertising finance), and Realtair (transaction workflow technology), and holds a controlling ~78% interest in REA India and a 20% stake in Move, Inc. (operator of realtor.com in the US, majority-owned by parent News Corp). REA is ~61% owned by News Corporation, which also owns Move Inc.'s other 80%, creating a structural relationship across REA's two largest markets.

business_model.summary: REA earns the large majority of revenue from subscription and depth-of-listing advertising fees charged to Australian real estate agents and developers for property listings on realestate.com.au and realcommercial.com.au, supplemented by a fast-growing Financial Services arm (Mortgage Choice broking commissions, PropTrack data licensing) and smaller adjacent businesses (CampaignAgent vendor-finance, Realtair, iGUIDE 3D tours). Since FY26, REA India (Housing.com/PropTiger) is presented as a discontinued operation following its planned sale to Aurum PropTech, so continuing-operations revenue is now almost entirely Australian residential/commercial property advertising plus Financial Services. Pricing power (a ~double-digit annual yield/price increase on subscriptions, e.g. an 8% Premiere+ price rise for FY27) has been the primary growth lever in recent years, more than offsetting flat-to-declining national listing volumes.
business_model.customer_type: B2B (real estate agents, developers, brokers, advertisers) funding the platform; B2C (property seekers, renters, buyers, share-house seekers) as the free audience side of the marketplace
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily Australia (~96%+ of continuing-operations revenue); REA India (Housing.com) is a discontinued operation being sold to Aurum PropTech (expected completion Q1 FY27, REA retaining a 24.9% stake in Aurum); 20% equity-accounted interest in Move Inc./realtor.com (US) held as an associate, not consolidated revenue

main_competitors: Domain Group (now owned by CoStar Group)
Move, Inc./realtor.com (US, REA's own associate, not a direct competitor to the AU business)
Zillow (US portal, competitor to associate Move Inc.)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant #1 residential and commercial property portal in Australia; effectively a duopoly with Domain, but REA has pulled decisively ahead — REA's monthly audience is roughly 5x Domain's on some measures, and REA attracted more site visits (~47.6m vs ~14.5m in one comparison) with 9 in 10 Australians who visit any property site visiting realestate.com.au

moat_factors.description: Largest audience of buyers/renters attracts agents who must list where the eyeballs are, and vice versa; scale gap versus Domain has been widening, reinforcing the flywheel

Agents view a realestate.com.au listing as close to mandatory for vendor outcomes, allowing REA to push through high-single to double-digit annual price increases even in flat-listing years (drew ACCC scrutiny)
PropTrack's proprietary AVM/valuation data (45+ years of property data) and REA's engagement metrics create a data advantage competitors struggle to replicate
realestate.com.au is the default, habitual first stop for Australian property search; half of monthly visitors use the platform exclusively
~61% News Corp ownership provides distribution/marketing support (e.g., placements in The Australian) but also raises governance/conflict considerations

weaknesses: Revenue concentrated almost entirely in Australian residential property advertising, making REA highly exposed to a single housing market cycle
Growth increasingly reliant on price increases rather than volume, drawing regulatory attention (ACCC) that could cap future pricing power
Consolidation of the market by CoStar's acquisition of Domain gives the #2 player a much larger, better-capitalised parent that could invest more aggressively in competing
International diversification has underperformed — REA India divested after a strategic review found the business could not achieve scale; Move Inc. stake is a minority, non-controlling position
Active litigation with Domain over allegedly misleading marketing claims (mutual counterclaims) creates legal/reputational overhang

growth_drivers: Continued yield growth via price increases and premium product upsell (Premiere+, Luxe, Pro subscription, Audience Maximiser) even as listing volumes plateau
AI-prime product roadmap ('Next Move' strategy) — conversational search, AI valuation tools, agentic property assistant — to deepen engagement and monetisation of the audience
Expansion of Financial Services (Mortgage Choice settlements up 13% YoY, PropTrack data contracts, new 70% stake in commercial lender Simplicity) diversifying revenue beyond core listings
Commercial and New Homes segment growth (+9% FY26) as a smaller, less penetrated adjacency
Bolt-on M&A in adjacent/immersive technology (61.5% stake in Planitar/iGUIDE for 3D tours, Neighbourlytics, Before You Buy, IMMERSIV) to extend the consumer/customer value proposition
Focus and simplification post-India exit allows management and capital to concentrate on the core, highly profitable Australian franchise
Ongoing capital returns (FY26 $200m buyback plus dividends, payout ratio risen to ~60%) supporting EPS growth and shareholder returns

business.description: FY27 buyer listings guided flat to down low-single-digits, concentrated weakness in Sydney/Melbourne (REA's highest-value markets); a sustained housing downturn directly reduces the advertising volume driving revenue

business.risk: Competitive intensity from a stronger Domain/CoStar
business.description: CoStar completed its ~A$2.5bn acquisition of Domain in August 2025, giving Domain access to a much larger, well-capitalised US parent that may invest aggressively to close the gap with REA

Real estate agents are REA's paying customers; agent pushback on pricing or platform terms (contract restriction clauses recently removed after ACCC pressure) could affect customer goodwill and negotiating leverage
Mutual Federal Court claims (REA vs Domain) over allegedly misleading marketing claims create legal costs and reputational risk

financial.description: Dividend payout ratio has risen from 54% (FY24) to 60% (FY26); continued high payouts plus buybacks reduce financial flexibility for reinvestment or downturns, though REA carries no net debt
Share of losses from associates (Move Inc. and others) was a $19-21m drag on EBITDA in FY26; US portal competitive dynamics can weigh on REA's equity-accounted earnings

regulatory.description: The ACCC opened a preliminary inquiry into REA's subscription pricing and market power, and REA has already given an undertaking to remove contract clauses that restricted agents from using rival platforms; further regulatory intervention could directly constrain REA's key pricing-power growth lever

regulatory.risk: Consumer/agent protection and data privacy law changes
regulatory.description: REA operates across multiple regulated domains (credit/financial services via Mortgage Choice/CampaignAgent, AML/CTF, data privacy) where compliance failures could bring fines or licence risk

regulatory.risk: Foreign regulatory approval risk on India divestment
regulatory.description: Sale of Housing.com to Aurum PropTech is subject to Aurum shareholder approval and other customary conditions, expected to complete by end of Q1 FY27 — deal could be delayed or renegotiated

macro.description: RBA rate settings directly affect buyer/vendor activity, clearance rates and listing volumes; markets were pricing meaningful probability of further rate rises as of September 2026, which could further dampen listings and transaction activity

macro.risk: Property market cyclicality / proposed tax changes
macro.description: Management specifically flagged interest rate rises, global unrest and proposed federal taxation changes (e.g., negative gearing/capital gains tax reform debate) as dampening buyer demand in H2 FY26
Reduced housing affordability and investor lending pullback could structurally lower transaction volumes over multiple years, independent of REA's execution

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian residential property portals form a near-duopoly (REA vs Domain/CoStar) with REA the dominant #1; industry growth now comes primarily from price/yield increases and monetisation of engagement (AI features, data products, premium subscriptions) rather than listing volume growth, which is forecast flat to modestly down in FY27
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately high — revenue is levered to Australian property transaction/listing volumes, which are sensitive to interest rates, buyer/seller confidence and government housing policy, though REA's subscription-style pricing model and product upsell provide some counter-cyclical buffering versus a pure transaction-fee model
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) — RBA cash rate changes affect mortgage affordability, buyer/seller activity, auction clearance rates and ultimately new listing volumes, REA's key top-line driver
key_input_costs: Technology/engineering talent and AI infrastructure investment
Marketing and brand spend (e.g., Australian Open sponsorship, Ready25 customer event)
M&A integration costs for bolt-on acquisitions

recent_developments.event: ACCC forced REA to remove contract clauses restricting agents from using rival listing platforms, following a preliminary inquiry into REA's subscription pricing and market power; no legal proceedings or finding of wrongdoing

FY26 Annual Report/Appendix 4E released: core continuing-operations revenue up 12% to $1,730.4m, core EBITDA (ex-associates) up 12% to $1,088m, core net profit from continuing operations up 14% to $682.1m; statutory net profit down 19% to $551.6m reflecting India impairment and the absence of a prior-year PropertyGuru gain; final dividend $1.73/share fully franked, total FY26 dividend $2.97/share (+20% YoY)

REA India announced sale of remaining business, Housing.com, to ASX/India-listed Aurum PropTech; on completion REA's stake in Aurum rises to 24.9%; transaction subject to Aurum shareholder approval, expected to complete by end of Q1 FY27
REA acquired 70% of Simplicity Loans & Advisory, a boutique commercial lending brokerage, extending Financial Services into commercial finance
PropTiger Marketing Services sold to Aurum PropTech (completed 25 September 2025); Housing Edge shut down in Q2 FY26 — the earlier steps in exiting the India business
New CEO Cameron McIntyre appointed following the retirement of long-serving CEO Owen Wilson; new CFO Andrew Cramer (ex-News Corp Deputy CFO) also joined during FY26
Acquired 61.5% controlling stake in Canadian 3D-tour/floorplan technology company Planitar Inc. (maker of iGUIDE), consolidated from 1 October 2025

Completed a $200 million on-market share buyback (launched February 2026), part of total shareholder returns of ~$546m for the year (buyback plus dividends), reflecting a strong, debt-free balance sheet
CoStar Group completed its ~A$2.5bn (US$1.6bn incremental) acquisition of Domain Group, REA's main domestic competitor, giving Domain access to a larger, better-capitalised parent
Federal Court litigation between REA and Domain over allegedly misleading marketing claims, with counterclaims from both sides

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results / Full Year Results presentation (August 2026)

items.notes: Weakness concentrated in Sydney and Melbourne, REA's highest-value markets

items.metric: Controllable residential Buy yield growth (ex-geo mix)
items.notes: Driven by an 8% Premiere+ price rise and add-on product growth, offsetting soft listing volumes
Group costs including M&A guided to rise mid-to-high single digits

items.vs_prior: maintained trajectory (FY26 EBITDA margin ~61% on core continuing revenue)
items.notes: Contributions from associates (e.g., Move Inc.) also expected to improve

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Cameron McIntyre and CFO Andrew Cramer emphasised entering FY27 with a healthy, debt-free balance sheet, sustained strength in the core Australian business, and a commitment to prudent cost management while executing the evolved 'Next Move' strategy (reinvent property experiences, scale growth engines in Commercial/New Homes/Financial Services/Global, accelerate the organisation via AI). Management explicitly flagged a more balanced/softening property market as FY26 progressed, with interest rate rises, global unrest and proposed federal tax changes dampening buyer demand in H2.

bull_case: Dominant, widening-lead market position in Australian property listings with strong two-sided network effects and pricing power that has consistently outpaced listing volume growth

High-margin, asset-light, debt-free business model generating strong free cash flow ($628m FY26, +17% YoY) funding both growth investment and substantial capital returns ($200m buyback plus ~60% dividend payout)

Simplified, more focused portfolio after divesting the loss-making/sub-scale India business, concentrating capital and management attention on the highly profitable Australian core plus adjacent Financial Services growth

Multiple monetisation levers beyond core listings — Financial Services (Mortgage Choice, PropTrack, Simplicity), Commercial/New Homes, and AI-driven product upsell — provide diversified paths to double-digit earnings growth even in a soft housing market
News Corp's ~61% ownership and shared exposure to Move Inc./realtor.com in the US provides alignment and potential for future consolidation optionality in the REA/Move relationship
bear_case: ACCC regulatory scrutiny of REA's subscription pricing and market power could directly cap the price-led yield growth that has been the primary earnings driver in a flat-listings environment

Domain, REA's main competitor, is now backed by CoStar Group's much larger balance sheet and could invest aggressively in product/marketing to close the audience and revenue gap, pressuring REA's pricing power over time

Revenue is heavily concentrated in a single housing market (Australia); FY27 guidance already points to declining listing volumes in Sydney and Melbourne amid rising interest rates and proposed tax reform, and a deeper property downturn would directly hit both volumes and vendor/agent willingness to pay premium prices

International diversification has largely failed — the India business was divested after strategic review, and the Move Inc. stake is a non-controlling minority position exposed to a highly competitive US portal market (Zillow, etc.)
Rising dividend payout ratio (60% in FY26) and ongoing buybacks reduce reinvestment flexibility if growth opportunities in AI/product innovation require larger capital commitments
